items.q: A web publisher can sell the same page view to several different ad slots on the same page.
items.why: A page usually holds several ad slots, and each slot is sold as its own impression.

items.q: An ads.txt file lists the sellers a publisher authorises to sell its inventory.
items.why: Buyers check ads.txt on the publisher domain to confirm a seller is authorised, which helps fight fraud.
items.hint: Think of it as a public list of approved sellers.

items.q: Lazy loading ads means every ad on the page loads at the same time as the page.
items.why: Lazy loading waits until a slot is close to the screen, so fewer ads load that are never seen.

items.q: Page speed has no effect on how many ad impressions a publisher earns.
items.why: Slow pages lose visitors and can delay ad calls, so fewer ads load and fewer are seen.

items.q: Cumulative layout shift is caused only by video ads.
items.why: Any ad or content that loads late and pushes the page around adds to layout shift, so reserving space for slots helps.

items.q: A sticky ad stays in view as the visitor scrolls, which can raise viewability.
items.why: Because the unit remains on screen longer, more of its impressions count as viewable.

items.q: Refreshing an ad slot every few seconds is always allowed by buyers and platforms.
items.why: Many platforms limit refresh and require the visitor to be active, because very fast refresh can inflate impressions.

items.q: Direct deals between a publisher and an advertiser can only be sold through an open auction.
items.why: Direct deals are agreed in advance, often at a fixed price, and bypass the open auction.

items.q: An app publisher cannot use the same ad formats that a web publisher uses.
items.why: Banner, interstitial and video formats exist on both, though the way they are requested and measured differs.

items.q: Connected TV ads are usually watched on a TV screen with a remote rather than a mouse, so they cannot be clicked in the usual way.
items.why: Viewers use a remote, so CTV is usually measured on completion and reach rather than clicks.

items.q: CTV and linear TV are the same thing delivered by a different cable.
items.why: Linear TV airs on a fixed schedule, while CTV streams over the internet and can target individual households.

items.q: In CTV, video completion rate is a common quality measure because ads are often not skippable.
items.why: Many CTV ads are served as full spots, so completion shows how many viewers watched to the end.

items.q: CTV impressions are always counted per person, not per household.
items.why: Most CTV reporting is at device or household level, because one screen is often shared.

items.q: A CTV ad pod is a group of ads played together in one commercial break.
items.why: Like a TV break, an ad pod holds several ads in a row, and each position can be sold separately.

items.q: Frequency capping matters less on CTV because viewers never see the same ad twice.
items.why: The same household can see the same ad repeatedly across apps, so capping across publishers is a real challenge.
